title: Short-circuit adminlets and idempotent microflows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight composable library of "adminlets" (small, permission-scoped admin utilities) plus an orchestration shim that turns runbooks into idempotent microflows. Goal: enable Support and SRE to execute common corrective actions with a safe, auditable fast path (short-circuit) that reduces mean time to resolution for high-frequency incidents while preserving SLOs and auditability. This work ties into our runbooks-as-tasks initiative but focuses on: (1) shrink-wrapped admin primitives, (2) idempotency and replay-safety for retries, (3) ephemeral credentialing for least-privilege execution, and (4) observability hooks for cost/latency accounting.
acceptance_criteria: A1: library of >=8 adminlets implemented (examples: rotate-ingress-key, clear-kv-prefix, restart-worker-pool, rehydrate-cache, reindex-embeddings, throttle-model-variant)
A2: all adminlets expose a consistent API: input schema, idempotency token, dry-run flag, and scoped-token header
A3: orchestration shim can convert an existing runbook step into a single microflow with dry-run and canary gates
A4: every executed microflow generates an immutable audit record (actor, params, result, request-id) to the Ops Audit stream
A5: retry semantics documented and tested: repeated identical requests with same idempotency token are no-op after success
A6: integration tests pass in CI for happy path, failure, and retry scenarios; e2e test against a staging cluster included
A7: security review completed and KMS-backed ephemeral signing of scoped tokens implemented
implementation_notes: Design adminlets as small Go binaries or lambda-style handlers behind the ops-agent service to keep binary size minimal and limit interaction surface
Use idempotency keys stored in a short-lived store (Redis with TTL) and fall back to monotonic operation logs for long-running ops
Short-circuit paths should bypass multi-step escalation for low-risk operations based on a configurable risk matrix (per-team policy)
Scoped ephemeral tokens are minted by Ops Controlplane and embedded as one-time bearer tokens with enforced TTL and auditable revocation
Prefer parameter schemas validated with JSON Schema; return structured result objects for Console to render (status, diagnostics, suggested rollback)
Cost/latency telemetry emitted via existing tracing and a new metric adminlet.latency_ms tagged by adminlet_name and team
testing_plan: Unit tests for each adminlet handler covering normal, edge, and error paths
Integration test harness in CI that spins up a minimal test cluster and exercises 6 nominal adminlets
Chaos test: inject transient failures (k8s API 503, kv timeouts) and assert idempotency guarantees on retry
Manual validation: Support team runbook dry-run day with guidance and canary opt-in
Security tests: token revocation, token replay attempts, and privilege escalation checks
rollout_plan: Stage: deploy adminlets to staging cluster behind feature-flag; enable dry-run only
Canary: invite Support engineers to opt-in and exercise real dry-runs; collect metrics for false positives
Gradual rollout: enable short-circuit execution for low-risk adminlets (risk=low) after 72h of canary stability
Full rollout: open to SRE + Support with RBAC mapping and 30-day audit retention; monitor error/SLO impact
Fallback: revoke ephemeral tokens and flip feature-flag if error rate > 2% or unexpected costs observed
